port_difficulty.why: No logic at all: opens, writes one record, closes. The only care is the COMP-3 amount field, and the record is written without ever being filled in.

blast_radius.why: Writes SPARQ.TEST.MASTER, the only shared dataset, on the must-not-break nightly path. Its output layout is a private copybook the reader does not share, so a break is silent.

units.driving_fact: Writes SPARQ.TEST.MASTER through LAYOUTX while the only reader, PGMR, describes the same bytes through LAYOUTY. The extractor rates that contract edge medium.

port_difficulty.why: Opens, reads one record, closes. It never uses a field of the record.

blast_radius.why: Writes nothing. It is on the must-not-break nightly path and reads a dataset whose layout it holds a private copy of. A layout drift would not fail it, because it never looks at the fields.

units.driving_fact: Reads SPARQ.TEST.MASTER through LAYOUTY, a copybook that differs by name from the writer's LAYOUTX. A medium contract edge crosses from PGMW to PGMR.

port_difficulty.why: One step. The work is in the DD: a new catalogued dataset with DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE), a one track allocation and an LRECL of 80 that neither copybook matches.

blast_radius.why: Creates the shared dataset. It is deleted on abend, so a failed run removes what the reader needs. A rerun without a delete step would fail on a duplicate name.

units.driving_fact: The OUTFILE DD carries RECFM=FB,LRECL=80. The record layout it feeds is 15 bytes by its PIC clauses. The extractor does not compare the two.

port_difficulty.why: One step, one DD with DISP=SHR, no DCB. It has nothing to convert.

blast_radius.why: It fails loudly if the dataset is missing. The order against WRITEJOB is not defined anywhere in the tree, because no scheduler was found.

units.driving_fact: Reads SPARQ.TEST.MASTER and depends on WRITEJOB having created it first. No scheduler artifact states that order.
